method: Re-underwrite the existing 2026-09-12 FULL_ANALYSIS using the canonical eight-category Harness scorecard plus a separate early-innovation archetype overlay based on patterns seen in early NVIDIA, Palantir, Tesla, Google and Amazon. The innovation overlay informs structural-change/moat judgments but never overrides owner-cash, dilution, capital-structure, valuation or Hard Veto constraints.
facts_used: Q2 diagnostics revenue $289.3M, +20% YoY; oncology test volume +31% YoY.
Q2 data and applications revenue $93.2M, +28% YoY; Insights/data licensing and modeling +36% YoY.
MRD volume rose to 9,000 tests in Q2 from about 6,500 in Q1; only a minority of the salesforce was selling MRD at the Q2 update.
Tempus signed about $200M of new Data and Applications licenses and delivered its first oncology foundation model to AstraZeneca.
Q2 gross profit increased 26% YoY, faster than revenue; adjusted EBITDA was +$8.0M and FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was about $65M.
Q2 GAAP net income included a $98.5M unrealized gain on marketable securities and $55.6M of stock-compensation expense and related payroll taxes.
H1 owner-cash diagnostic used in prior Harness review: OCF -$80.802M minus PP&E $14.327M minus SBC $106.827M = about -$201.956M before additional capitalized-software deduction.
Cash and marketable securities were about $820.7M at June 30, 2026; convertible senior notes net were about $1.173B and a convertible promissory note about $187.9M.
Personalis acquisition announced at about $1.5B enterprise value remained a material capital-allocation and dilution/claim uncertainty in the current evidence set.

Current canonical valuation at $59.01 reference price: Bear $2.27, Base $57.66, Bull $254.01; reverse-required uniform years-2-10 revenue growth about 16.27% conditional on Base margins/capital claims/terminal assumptions.

category_creation_and_structural_change.reason: AI-enabled precision oncology, multimodal diagnostics and data/model licensing can enlarge the precision-medicine market rather than merely take share.

product_market_fit_and_adoption.reason: Oncology volume +31%, MRD sequential acceleration and 36% Insights growth provide direct customer-adoption evidence.

data_network_ecosystem_flywheel.reason: More diagnostic tests create multimodal clinical/molecular data; the data improve models and pharma value, which can drive partnerships, reimbursement and more diagnostic adoption. Exclusivity and retention are not yet proven enough for a maximum score.

scale_economics.reason: Gross profit and adjusted EBITDA are improving, but SBC-adjusted owner cash is still materially negative and acquisitions are important to expansion.

tam_and_share_runway.reason: MRD, oncology diagnostics, hereditary testing, clinical-trial/data licensing and AI models provide multiple large adjacent markets.

founder_management_reinvestment.reason: Founder-led strategic coherence is visible, but acquisition intensity and convertible financing require proof of per-share value creation.

survivability.reason: Liquidity is substantial and adjusted EBITDA is inflecting positive, but convertible claims and acquisition commitments make the balance sheet more complex.

power_law_optionality.reason: A successful clinical-data flywheel can create a much larger platform, but permanent-loss downside remains large if cash conversion or data moat fails.

archetype_similarity.Google: HIGH - strongest analogy is a data feedback loop in which product usage creates proprietary data that improves subsequent products and monetization.
archetype_similarity.Palantir: HIGH - similar potential to embed data/AI into high-value institutional workflows, but Tempus has less disclosed evidence of NRR-like expansion and workflow lock-in.
archetype_similarity.Amazon: MODERATE_HIGH - aggressive reinvestment and adjacency expansion can deepen the platform, but Tempus relies more heavily on acquisitions and regulated clinical reimbursement.
archetype_similarity.NVIDIA: MODERATE - it can become a platform for precision-medicine AI, but it does not yet have a CUDA-like developer ecosystem or de facto technical standard.
archetype_similarity.Tesla: MODERATE_LOW - there is vertical integration across diagnostics, data and models, but less evidence of a manufacturing learning curve that structurally lowers unit cost.

evidence: Oncology/MRD adoption and data-model licensing are scaling at the same time.
First oncology foundation model delivered to AstraZeneca demonstrates movement from data vendor toward model/platform provider.
counter_evidence: Precision oncology remains highly competitive and category leadership is not equivalent to a standard or monopoly.

evidence: 31% oncology volume growth, MRD acceleration, FDA approval and data-license signings indicate clinical and pharma willingness to pay.
counter_evidence: Reimbursement, payer collection and proof that AI models improve measurable outcomes remain important.

evidence: Diagnostics generate multimodal data that can improve models and data products; pharma relationships and clinical adoption can then reinforce diagnostics.
MRD, data licensing and foundation-model delivery broaden the platform beyond one test type.
counter_evidence: Data may not be fully exclusive; competing diagnostics/data platforms can build overlapping datasets; M&A is contributing to the breadth.

evidence: Q2 gross profit grew 26% versus 22% revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA turned positive.
counter_evidence: H1 SBC-adjusted owner-cash diagnostic remains about -$202M before capitalized software; economic investment cohorts and Personalis return are not proven.

evidence: Founder-led strategy links diagnostics, MRD, data licensing and AI models into one platform; capital is being deployed into adjacent capabilities with clear strategic logic.
counter_evidence: Large acquisitions and convertible financing can create empire-building, dilution or sub-hurdle ROIC; strategic fit does not prove per-share value creation.

evidence: About $820.7M cash and marketable securities and positive adjusted-EBITDA trajectory reduce near-term financing pressure.
counter_evidence: Convertible notes and promissory-note claims are large relative to current cash generation and Personalis increases capital-structure complexity.

evidence: Reference price $59.01 is approximately equal to prior Base $57.66 and far below modeled Bull $254.01.
Reverse-required years-2-10 growth around 16.27% is demanding but not obviously inconsistent with current adoption if Base margin conversion occurs.
counter_evidence: Base requires a large owner-cash inflection that is not yet observed; terminal value dominates the model and Bear value is only about $2.27.

evidence: Bull is over 4x reference price and a successful data/platform flywheel could expand across multiple precision-medicine markets.
counter_evidence: Bear implies near-total permanent loss if the company fails to convert growth into per-share cash while claims and dilution accumulate.

score_change_explanation: The prior 54 score underweighted directly observed adoption and the diagnostics->multimodal data->AI models/pharma->diagnostics flywheel. The re-underwrite therefore raises structural change, customer value and moat trajectory materially. It does not treat innovation as a substitute for cash economics: incremental ROIC/FCF-share, capital allocation, survivability and valuation remain restrained.
permanent_loss_case: Tempus can remain clinically relevant and still be a poor stock if diagnostics/data growth requires persistent SBC, acquisition capital and convertible claims, if payer cash collection lags, or if competing platforms prevent proprietary-data advantages from widening. In that case revenue can grow while owner cash per diluted share remains negative and the valuation compresses toward a small fraction of current price.
falsifiers: Oncology/MRD volume remains strong but Data and Applications/Insights growth decelerates materially, weakening evidence that diagnostics create a valuable data flywheel.
Two or more reporting periods of revenue growth without clear improvement in SBC-adjusted owner cash per diluted share.
Personalis or other acquisition cohorts require repeated external financing or fail to generate returns above the required hurdle after integration.
Payer collection/reimbursement economics deteriorate such that volume growth does not translate into cash gross profit.
Foundation-model/data-license wins remain isolated projects rather than repeatable expansions across pharmaceutical customers.
Diluted share count or equity-linked claims increase materially faster than owner-cash value creation.
increase_evidence: At least two reporting periods with oncology/MRD volume growth, Insights/data licensing growth and SBC-adjusted owner cash per share improving together.
Evidence of repeat or expanding data/model contracts across pharma customers, analogous to NRR or cohort expansion.
Personalis integration creates higher MRD adoption and cash contribution without disproportionate dilution or leverage.
Gross-margin/EBITDA leverage translates into positive owner cash after SBC, capex, capitalized software and working-capital normalization.
Updated reverse DCF remains below a defensible long-run platform growth path after fully incorporating dilution and convertible claims.
sell_evidence: Data flywheel fails: diagnostic growth no longer improves data/model monetization or vice versa.
Persistent negative owner cash per share despite slowing acquisition/reinvestment intensity.
Material shareholder dilution or debt/equity claims accumulate without proportional per-share owner cash.
Major reimbursement, regulatory, data-access or clinical-adoption impairment.
Price rises to require Bull-or-better execution before cash economics are proven.
valuation_action: UNCHANGED; innovation overlay changes probability judgment and score, not the existing Bear/Base/Bull cash model without new cash-flow evidence.
